findings.title: A web page could make a bot open oxbot's own page and create a pairing code
findings.problem: The policy let bots open any http(s) address, including http://127.0.0.1:7878. That page counts as the Farm (its Origin is local), so a bot steered by a web page could click 'Show pairing code', read the link and send it out; anyone on the Wi-Fi could then pair as Jay for good.
findings.fix: Bots may no longer open pages on this Mac or the home network (localhost, 127.x, private and link-local addresses, .local and dot-less names, IPv6 local). Same rule for request_sign_in. Tests added (crates/oxbot-browser/src/web.rs, policy.rs).

findings.title: The QR scanner pulled in Google Play services (ML Kit)
findings.problem: tauri-plugin-barcode-scanner depends on com.google.android.gms:play-services-mlkit-barcode-scanning, which talks to Google. That breaks the data rule (Claude/Codex and the Farm only).
findings.fix: Removed the plugin. The phone reads camera frames in its WebView and decodes them in the app's Rust side with rqrr (pure Rust). Checked: the APK has no gms or mlkit classes.

findings.title: An older `oxbot chat` would stop on the new Gates message
findings.problem: Every Farm connection was sent {type: gates} even with no Gates; an older chat client can't read that kind and quits. (Reviewer rated Critical; downgraded: only when the CLI is older than the server.)
findings.fix: chat.rs now skips kinds it doesn't know; the server sends Gates on connect only once a Gate exists.

findings.title: 'The Farm' is still decided by the page's Origin (127.0.0.1)
findings.problem: Any page or program on this Mac that reaches 127.0.0.1:7878 counts as the owner: a bot that clicks a link to 127.0.0.1 (not covered by C1, which blocks opening pages), another local program, or a page on another localhost port. It can approve red cards and start pairing.
findings.fix: Give the real Farm window a secret: the desktop app opens the page with a random token (kept in a cookie for that window); without it a local connection is a guest, not the Farm. Also ask in a native Mac dialog before every new pairing, and show every pairing to all Farm windows.

findings.title: The Gate door listens on every network the Mac joins
findings.problem: It binds 0.0.0.0:7879 and announces itself (Mac name and fingerprint) over mDNS on every interface, also on café or office Wi-Fi and VPNs, whenever a Gate is paired.
findings.fix: Accept only private-address peers; open the door only on networks marked as home (remember the router), close it elsewhere and when no Gates are left; let the owner pick the announced name.

findings.title: Anyone who can see a bot can answer its red cards
findings.problem: On a shared bot or Herder, Sam's phone can approve a card raised by Jay's request. The first tap wins.
findings.fix: Only the person whose turn raised the card, and the Farm, see and answer it (store the asker on the approval).

findings.title: Herder and shared bots keep one conversation for everyone
findings.problem: With Gates, several people talk to the same Claude session; one can ask what another asked. Only the prompt says not to share.
findings.fix: A separate Herder session per person (runtime keyed by bot and person), or reset when the person changes.

findings.title: The door's accept loop never stops after closing
findings.problem: It waits in accept() holding port 7879, so stop then start in one process fails with 'port taken' and a task leaks.
findings.fix: select! on tx.closed() alongside accept().

findings.title: Opening the door twice at once fails or leaks
findings.problem: Two quick 'Show pairing code' clicks: the second bind fails on 7879 (false error) or a second mDNS daemon is left running.
findings.fix: Serialize open() with an async mutex; start mDNS only after winning.

findings.title: Unlimited TLS handshakes
findings.problem: Each TCP connection spawns a 10 s handshake task with no cap; one LAN device can run the Farm out of file handles.
findings.fix: Semaphore (e.g. 64), 5 s handshake timeout, header/idle timeouts on the unauthenticated routes.

findings.title: The Farm never notices a phone that walked away
findings.problem: No ping or idle timeout on Gate sockets, so a phone out of range shows 'connected now' for a long time.
findings.fix: Close Gate sockets after ~60 s without a frame (the phone already pings every 15 s).

findings.title: 'Online' count can drift
findings.problem: set_online(false) isn't tied to a guard; a panic leaves the Gate online forever.
findings.fix: A guard struct that marks it offline in Drop.

findings.title: A removal can be missed
findings.problem: The removal listener subscribes after the upgrade, and lagged messages are skipped, so a removed Gate may stay connected.
findings.fix: After subscribing and on Lagged, re-check the Gate still exists.

findings.title: The phone can load the Farm page twice
findings.problem: Timer, Try again, online and visibility events can all start open() at once; a second swap breaks the page.
findings.fix: An 'opening' guard and clearTimeout at the start of open().

findings.title: A message typed while offline is lost
findings.problem: Enter still submits; send() drops it silently and the box is cleared.
findings.fix: Keep the text and show 'Not connected yet' (or queue and send on reconnect).

findings.title: Farm-only check is a separate list that allows by default
findings.problem: A new Farm-only message not added to farm_only() would run for a Gate.
findings.fix: List every ClientMsg variant with no catch-all, or check inside each handler.

findings.title: door.rs does eight jobs
findings.problem: Certificate, codes, TLS listener, mDNS, QR, presence and HTTP handlers in one 700-line file; the risky code-tries logic can't be unit-tested alone.
findings.fix: Split into door/{identity,pairing,listener,discovery,http}.rs with a pure PairingCodes type.

findings.title: door and server depend on each other; Hub hands out its whole Store
findings.problem: Any module can now write SQLite directly, bypassing the Hub's who-sees-what rules.
findings.fix: Narrow Hub methods for Gates, remove Hub::store(), pass the router into Door::open.

findings.title: A database hiccup makes the phone forget its pairing
findings.problem: check_key turns any DB error into 401 'not paired', and the phone deletes its saved pairing.
findings.fix: 503 on DB errors; 401 only when the key really isn't known.

findings.title: The link format and fingerprint code exist twice
findings.problem: pair_link and PairLink::parse, fingerprint() and 'oxbot-farm' are defined on both sides; one change silently breaks pairing.
findings.fix: One owner (oxbot-gate) for the link format, fingerprint and certificate name; oxbot depends on it.

findings.title: Security settings live in hand-edited generated Android files
findings.problem: allowBackup, the local-network permission request and CAMERA are edits to files 'tauri android init' regenerates.
findings.fix: A small local Tauri plugin for these, or a documented re-apply step plus a check.

findings.title: Docs still say Gates come later
findings.problem: README, the C4 page and a server comment don't show the Gate door, the phone app or OXBOT_GATE_PORT.
findings.fix: Update README and the C4 diagrams; add the Android build steps.

findings.title: Home-made HTTP client swallows read errors
findings.problem: A cut-off answer can be parsed as complete; a kept-open connection waits 30 s.
findings.fix: Use hyper's client over the pinned TLS stream (already in the lockfile).

findings.title: Risky paths have no tests
findings.problem: Code expiry, 5 wrong tries, cancel, close and reopen, concurrent open, the scanner and the Gates tab.
findings.fix: Unit tests for PairingCodes with an injected clock; e2e flow for the Gates tab.

findings.title: Reconnect logic is written twice
findings.problem: gate.html's listeners stay after the swap; two retry loops can fight.
findings.fix: Let the phone's socket stand-in own reconnecting; remove gate.html listeners on swap; move the Gates tab into its own script.

findings.title: No off switch for the door
findings.problem: OXBOT_GATE_PORT=0 means 'any port'; the door stays open after the last Gate is removed.
findings.fix: OXBOT_GATE_PORT=off; close when no Gates and no code.

findings.title: The phone's saved pairing has no version and isn't written safely
findings.problem: A format change or a crash mid-write silently unpairs the phone.
findings.fix: Version field, write to a temp file and rename, show load errors.

findings.title: Who a Gate belongs to is free text
findings.problem: 'sam' and 'Sam' become two people; names with brackets go into prompts.
findings.fix: Pick from existing people (case-insensitive), refuse reserved names and brackets, cap length.

findings.title: A phone can pretend a line came from someone else
findings.problem: Text like 'hi\n[Jay] …' looks like a message from Jay to the bot.
findings.fix: Escape '[' at line starts in deliver(), or a per-turn delimited sender header.

findings.title: The Farm page on the phone can call every app command
findings.problem: No command allowlist or CSP; PairLink accepts any host, so a bug in the page could re-pair the phone to another server.
findings.fix: Allow only gate_open/send/close after the swap; private hosts only in PairLink; a CSP.

findings.title: Phone-to-phone transfer can copy the key
findings.problem: allowBackup=false doesn't cover device transfer on Android 12+; debug builds allow run-as.
findings.fix: dataExtractionRules excluding everything; release build; Keystore (planned).

findings.title: The key is in a plain app file, not the Keystore
findings.problem: The crate says 'secure storage'; the app writes farm.json. Planned for later.
findings.fix: Move to Android Keystore, or document the decision.
